definition: An actual (all-in) position is exposure to the outright physical price of gas at one location; a basis position is exposure only to the spread between two locations' prices.
core_idea: Because a basis price is itself a spread, holding a basis position means being simultaneously exposed to two locations rather than to an outright price level.
key_points: An actual/all-in position: e.g., a trader physically owning gas at a location is exposed to that location's outright price.
A basis position: exposure to the difference between the basis location's price and the index (Henry Hub) location's price.
A long basis position at a location (e.g., Waha) is economically equivalent to physically owning gas at that location while being obligated to deliver gas at Henry Hub.
relationships: Basis positions are built from the same basis-price definition as the pricing terminology item.
Basis positions are typically executed via a Henry Hub futures trade plus a basis swap.
trading_implications: A long basis position isolates locational spread risk without taking outright Henry Hub price risk, since the position nets against an implied Henry Hub delivery obligation.
caveats: Confusing a basis position (spread exposure, two locations) with an actual position (outright exposure, one location).
